newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill market quiet as banks stay away.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill market quiet as banks stay away.

text.p: Philippine banks kept away from the secondary treasury bills market in view of the uncertainties over the liquidity situation, traders said.
On Monday, the central bank lifted its overnight lending rate to 26 percent from 22 percent in line with the higher demand for pesos to build liquidity.
The central bank last week raised liquidity reserves by two percentage points to stop banks from further speculating on the peso.
"The uncertainty (on liquidity) is still there. So there's no activity in the secondary market," a foreign bank dealer said.
"There are more sellers than buyers of bills in the market. The number of borrowers in the market have grown," another trader said.
He said banks expected an increase of 50 to 75 basis points in the T-bill auction later. That prompted banks to quote higher bid and offer rates at the secondary market, he said.
The average interbank call loan rate rose to 20.625 percent from 20.0625 percent as banks covered their weekend positions.
Volume swelled to 27.53 billion pesos from 20.06 billion, with 27 lenders and 23 borrowers.
